definition: Self-reward is the process of giving oneself positive reinforcement or acknowledgment. In the self-control model of depression, reduced self-reward is described as one of the self-regulation problems associated with depressive symptoms.

reasons: The packet supports only that the self-control model of depression includes reduced self-reward as one factor; it does not define self-reward as giving oneself positive reinforcement or acknowledgment.
The added claim that reduced self-reward is a self-regulation problem associated with depressive symptoms goes beyond the packet’s wording and should not be presented as a general definition.
The packet does not define “self-reward” as “giving oneself positive reinforcement or acknowledgment”; it only mentions “reduced self-reward” within the self-control model of depression.

The packet does not state that “reduced self-reward” is “one of the self-regulation problems” associated with depressive symptoms; it describes reduced self-reward as part of factors the self-control model proposes underlying depressive symptoms, without using that “self-regulation problems” phrasing.
